questions.question: Who has been chosen for the Indira Gandhi Prize for Peace, Disarmament and Development for the year 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Michelle Bachelet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indira Gandhi Prize for Peace, Disarmament and Development** for the year **2024** has been awarded to **Michelle Bachelet**, the former President of **Chile**.
 
• She was selected for the prestigious award by an international jury chaired by the former Vice-President of India, **M. Hamid Ansari**.
 
• The award recognizes her "extraordinary contribution" to **human rights**, **gender equality**, and her leadership in **global health** and **poverty alleviation**.
 
• **Michelle Bachelet** made history as the **first female President of Chile**, serving two non-consecutive terms from **2006 to 2010** and **2014 to 2018**.
 
• She was also the inaugural Executive Director of **UN Women** (United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women) and served as the **United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights** from **2018 to 2022**.
 
• The **Indira Gandhi Memorial Trust** noted her lifelong commitment to democratic values and her work in defending the rights of the marginalized and vulnerable populations worldwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Indira Gandhi Prize for Peace, Disarmament and Development:**
 
 
• This prestigious award was instituted in **1986** by the **Indira Gandhi Memorial Trust** in memory of the former Prime Minister of India.
 
• It is awarded annually to individuals or organizations that have made outstanding contributions toward promoting **international peace**, **disarmament**, and a **new international economic order**.
 
• The prize carries a cash award of **₹25 lakh** and a citation.
 
• Past recipients include world leaders and organizations such as **Mikhail Gorbachev**, **Nelson Mandela**, **UNICEF**, **ISRO**, and **Jimmy Carter**.
 
• In **2023**, the prize was jointly awarded to classical pianist **Daniel Barenboim** and peace activist **Ali Abu Awwad** for their efforts in the **Middle East**.
 
 
 
• **Michelle Bachelet's Background:**
 
 
• Born on **September 29, 1951**, in **Santiago, Chile**, she is a physician by training with a specialization in **Pediatrics** and **Public Health**.
 
• Before her presidency, she served as Chile's **Minister of Health** and **Minister of National Defense**, becoming the first woman in **Latin America** to hold a defense portfolio.
 
• During her tenure as President, she introduced significant **social reforms**, including the expansion of **childcare** and **pension systems** to support the elderly and the poor.
 
• Her leadership during the **2010 earthquake** in Chile and her efforts to rebuild the nation were highly commended internationally.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The prize highlights the intersection of **development** and **peace**, emphasizing that sustainable growth is impossible without a stable and equitable global environment.
 
• **Michelle Bachelet** is the **second Chilean** to be associated with high-level international peace recognition in recent years, reinforcing the country's role in global diplomacy.
 
• The selection of a former **UN High Commissioner for Human Rights** underscores the **Indira Gandhi Memorial Trust's** focus on **multilateralism** and the protection of civil liberties in the **21st century**.
 
• The award ceremony typically takes place in **New Delhi**, where the citation is presented by the Chairperson of the Trust.

questions.question: Which country along with Indian Air Force conducted their first-ever joint special operations exercise, 'Tiger Claw', from 26 May to 10 June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United States of America**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **'Tiger Claw'** exercise is a significant milestone as it marks the **first-ever joint special operations exercise** specifically involving the **Indian Air Force (IAF)** and the **United States of America**.
 
• This strategic engagement was conducted from **26 May to 10 June 2025**, focusing on the integration of elite special forces and aerial warfare tactics. ***Hence, the statement regarding the country and the exercise name is correct.***
 
• The primary objective of **'Tiger Claw'** is to enhance **interoperability** between the special operations units of both nations, facilitating the exchange of best practices in **counter-terrorism**, **unconventional warfare**, and **behind-enemy-lines operations**.
 
• The **Indian Air Force** deployed its specialized **Garud Commando Force**, while the **United States** participated with its highly trained **Special Operations Command (SOCOM)** units.
 
• The exercise underscores the deepening **strategic partnership** and defense cooperation between **India** and the **USA** in the **Indo-Pacific region**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **List of Important India-USA Joint Exercises:**
 
 
• **Yudh Abhyas:** An annual **Army-to-Army** exercise aimed at enhancing cooperation and interoperability.
 
• **Vajra Prahar:** A specific **Special Forces** exercise conducted between the **Indian Army** and the **US Army** special units.
 
• **Cope India:** A series of **Air Force** exercises that focus on enhancing operational capabilities and tactical skills of the **IAF** and the **USAF**.
 
• **Malabar:** Originally a bilateral **Naval exercise** between **India** and the **USA**, it now includes **Japan** and **Australia** (the **QUAD** nations).
 
• **Tiger Triumph:** A **tri-service** humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) exercise launched in **2019**.
 
 
 
• **Defense Cooperation:** In **2016**, the **United States** designated **India** as a **Major Defense Partner (MDP)**, which elevated the defense relationship to a level commensurate with its closest allies.
 
• **Garud Commando Force:** Formed in **September 2004**, it is the **special forces** unit of the **Indian Air Force** tasked with **protection of critical airfields**, **search and rescue**, and **counter-terrorism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Foundational Agreements:** The defense relationship is bolstered by four foundational agreements signed between **India** and the **USA**:
 
 
• **GSOMIA (2002):** General Security of Military Information Agreement.
 
• **LEMOA (2016):** Logistics Exchange Memorandum of Agreement.
 
• **COMCASA (2018):** Communications Compatibility and Security Agreement.
 
• **BECA (2020):** Basic Exchange and Cooperation Agreement for Geo-Spatial Cooperation.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitical Context:** Exercises like **'Tiger Claw'** are crucial for maintaining **security and stability** in the **Indo-Pacific**, addressing shared threats such as maritime piracy and territorial aggression.
 
• **Technology Sharing:** The **Defense Technology and Trade Initiative (DTTI)** serves as a mechanism to facilitate **co-development** and **co-production** of defense equipment between the two nations.
</ul

questions.question: Which organisation typically supports the implementation of the 'Sports and Games for the Disabled' scheme?

options.text: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** is the primary nodal agency in **India** responsible for the formulation and implementation of policies related to sports development, including the specialized scheme for **Sports and Games for the Disabled**.
 
• The main objective of this scheme is to promote **broad-basing of sports** among **differently-abled** persons (**Divyangjan**) by providing them with opportunities to participate in competitive sports and physical activities.
 
• Under this initiative, the **Government of India** provides financial assistance for the organization of **National Coaching Camps**, procurement of specialized sports equipment, and the conduct of **State and National level competitions**.
 
• The scheme specifically targets three categories of disabled athletes: the **Orthopedically Impaired**, the **Visually Impaired**, and those with **Intellectual Disabilities** (formerly referred to as Mentally Retallenged).
 
• The implementation is carried out through various specialized sports bodies such as the **Paralympic Committee of India (PCI)**, **Special Olympics Bharat**, and the **All India Sports Council of the Deaf (AISCD)**, all of which receive grants from the **Ministry**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Integration with Khelo India:**
 
 
• In recent years, the standalone scheme for the disabled has been integrated as a specific vertical under the **Khelo India - National Programme for Development of Sports**.
 
• This vertical, titled **"Promotion of sports among persons with disabilities,"** ensures a more streamlined flow of **funds** and better **infrastructure** access for para-athletes across the **country**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Sports Authority of India (SAI):**
 
 
• The **Sports Authority of India**, an autonomous body under the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, provides the necessary technical support and **training facilities** for athletes selected under these schemes.
 
• **SAI** centers across **India** are increasingly becoming **barrier-free** to accommodate the unique needs of disabled sports persons.
 
 
 
• **International Participation:**
 
 
• The ministry facilitates the participation of Indian contingents in major international events such as the **Paralympic Games**, **Asian Para Games**, and the **Special Olympics World Games**.
 
• Financial support for international exposure is provided through the **Scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legislative Context:** The promotion of sports for the disabled aligns with the mandates of the **Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016**, which emphasizes **equality** and **non-discrimination** in the fields of culture, leisure, and **sports**.
 
• **Annual Calendar of Training and Competitions (ACTC):** The **Ministry** approves a specific **ACTC** for para-sports every **year**, ensuring that athletes have a fixed schedule for **training** and **tournaments** with dedicated **budgets**.
 
• **Recognition:** Successful para-athletes are eligible for prestigious national honors such as the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** and the **Arjuna Award**, further incentivizing excellence in **disabled sports**.
 
• **Cash Incentives:** Under the **Scheme of Special Awards**, the **Ministry** grants significant **monetary rewards** to medal winners at international championships to recognize their **achievements** and provide **financial security**.
</ul

questions.question: Who took oath as the ninth Chief Minister of Delhi at the Ramlila Maidan on 20 February 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rekha Gupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rekha Gupta** took the oath as the **ninth Chief Minister** of the National Capital Territory (NCT) of **Delhi**.
 
• The swearing-in ceremony was held on **20 February 2025** at the historic **Ramlila Maidan**, a venue synonymous with major political shifts in India's capital.
 
• She represents the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**, which emerged victorious in the **2025 Delhi Legislative Assembly elections**.
 
• The oath of office and secrecy was administered by the **Lieutenant Governor (L-G)** of Delhi, acting on behalf of the **President of India**.
 
• By assuming this office, **Rekha Gupta** became the **fourth woman** to serve as the Chief Minister of Delhi, following in the footsteps of **Sushma Swaraj**, **Sheila Dikshit**, and **Atishi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Political Career of Rekha Gupta:**
 
 
• She began her political journey as a student leader with the **Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP)** and served as the **General Secretary** of the **Delhi University Students' Union (DUSU)** in **1996-97**.
 
• She has been a prominent face in the **Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD)**, serving as a **Councillor** from the **Shalimar Bagh** ward for multiple terms.
 
• She also held the position of **Member** of the **Standing Committee** in the MCD and has been a member of the **BJP National Executive**.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Framework:**
 
 
• The governance of Delhi is governed by **Article 239AA** of the **Indian Constitution**, inserted by the **69th Amendment Act, 1991**.
 
• This article provides the **Union Territory of Delhi** with a **Legislative Assembly** and a **Council of Ministers** headed by a Chief Minister.
 
• The **Delhi Legislative Assembly** has **70 seats**, and the **tenure** of the house is **five years** unless dissolved earlier.
 
 
 
• **History of Chief Ministers in Delhi:**
 
 
• The post was first established in **1952** (with **Brahm Prakash** as the first CM) but was abolished in **1956** and later reinstated in **1993**.
 
• **Sheila Dikshit** remains the longest-serving Chief Minister of Delhi, holding the office for **15 years** from **1998 to 2013**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Administrative Significance:** Under the **GNCTD (Amendment) Act**, the **Chief Minister** of Delhi leads the executive, but powers regarding **Public Order**, **Police**, and **Land** remain with the **Central Government** via the **Lieutenant Governor**.
 
• **Election Context:** The **2025 Delhi Elections** saw a high voter turnout across **70 constituencies**, where the **BJP** secured a majority, surpassing the **halfway mark of 36 seats** to form the government.
 
• **Venue History:** **Ramlila Maidan**, where the oath took place, has been the site of the **JP Movement (1975)** and the **Anna Hazare anti-corruption crusade (2011)**, making it a symbolic choice for the **2025** transition of power.
</ul

questions.question: When did South Korea host the World Environment Day in 2025, as designated by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 June**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **World Environment Day** is celebrated globally every year on **5 June**. This date was established by the **United Nations** to encourage worldwide awareness and action for the protection of the environment. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• For the year **2025**, the **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)** designated the **Republic of Korea (South Korea)** as the global host for World Environment Day.
 
• The **2025** celebration in **South Korea** aims to highlight the urgency of ending **plastic pollution** and fostering global sustainability.
 
• The event is particularly significant as it precedes the potential conclusion of a global, legally binding instrument on **plastic pollution**, for which **South Korea** also hosted the fifth session of the **Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC-5)**.
 
• The primary goal of **World Environment Day 2025** is to underscore the importance of a **circular economy** and the reduction of plastic waste on a global scale.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History of World Environment Day:**
 
 
• It was established by the **UN General Assembly** in **1972** on the first day of the **Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment**.
 
• The first-ever World Environment Day was celebrated in **1973** with the theme "**Only One Earth**".
 
 
 
• **UN Environment Programme (UNEP):**
 
 
• **UNEP** is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda and promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the **United Nations** system.
 
• The headquarters of **UNEP** is located in **Nairobi, Kenya**. It was founded by **Maurice Strong** in **June 1972**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Other Dates:**
 
 
• **22 April**: This date is celebrated as **Earth Day** (International Mother Earth Day), which focuses on broader environmental issues and climate literacy.
 
• **8 June**: This date is observed as **World Oceans Day**, dedicated to celebrating the role of the oceans in our everyday lives and inspiring action to protect them.
 
• **5 May**: While not the World Environment Day, **5 May** is occasionally associated with regional environmental observances or national days in various countries, such as **Children's Day** in **South Korea** and **Japan**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Recent Hosts and Themes:**
 
 
• **2024 Host**: **Saudi Arabia** hosted the event with a focus on **land restoration, desertification, and drought resilience**.
 
• **2023 Host**: **Côte d'Ivoire** (in partnership with the **Netherlands**) hosted the day with the theme "**Solutions to Plastic Pollution**".
 
• **2018 Host**: **India** hosted the global event with the theme "**Beat Plastic Pollution**", leading to a significant domestic commitment to ban single-use plastics.
 
 
 
• **Global Impact**: **World Environment Day** has grown to be the largest global platform for environmental public outreach, with millions of people from over **150 countries** participating in activities to protect the planet.

questions.question: As per the Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025, population covered by social protection systems has increased to which level in 2025, indicating substantial expansion in social security coverage in the country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**64.3%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework (NIF) Progress Report, 2025**, released by the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**, provides a comprehensive overview of India’s progress toward the **2030 Agenda**.
 
• According to the **2025** report, the percentage of the population covered by **social protection systems** or floors has seen a substantial increase, reaching **64.3%**.
 
• This indicator is specifically linked to **SDG Target 1.3**, which focuses on implementing nationally appropriate social protection systems and measures for all, including floors, to achieve substantial coverage of the poor and the vulnerable.
 
• The expansion to **64.3%** reflects the successful scaling of various **government-led interventions** designed to provide a safety net against economic and social risks.
 
• The **National Indicator Framework (NIF)** serves as the backbone for monitoring **SDGs** in India, currently tracking **284 indicators** across all **17 Sustainable Development Goals**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Social Protection Systems:**
 
 
• These systems encompass a set of policies and programs designed to reduce **poverty** and vulnerability by promoting efficient labour markets and enhancing the capacity of individuals to manage risks such as **sickness**, **disability**, **unemployment**, and **old age**.
 
• In India, this includes major schemes such as the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**, **PM-KISAN**, and various **pension schemes** for the elderly and widowed.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goal 1 (No Poverty):**
 
 
• **SDG 1** aims to end poverty in all its forms everywhere. **Indicator 1.3.1** specifically tracks the proportion of the population covered by social protection floors/systems, disaggregated by sex and key vulnerable groups.
 
• The **2025 report** indicates that India is moving closer to its targets through **digital transformation** and **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **Role of MoSPI:**
 
 
• The **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** is the nodal agency for the **Sustainable Development Goals** indicators in India.
 
• It collaborates with various **Central Ministries** and **State Governments** to collect and validate data for the **National Indicator Framework**.
 
 
 
• **Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI):**
 
 
• The expansion of social security coverage to **64.3%** is largely attributed to the **JAM Trinity** (Jan Dhan, Aadhaar, and Mobile), which has streamlined the identification and delivery of benefits to the **unorganized sector**.
 
• The **e-Shram portal** has also played a pivotal role in registering over **29 crore unorganized workers**, facilitating their inclusion into the national social security net.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Target 1.3 Implementation:** India’s approach to social protection is multi-layered, covering **health insurance** through **Ayushman Bharat**, **life insurance** through **PMJJBY**, and **accidental insurance** through **PMSBY**.
 
• **Impact of the 2025 Report:** The report serves as a critical tool for **policy makers** to identify gaps in service delivery and re-allocate resources to states or sectors that are lagging in **social security** reach.
 
• **Global Comparison:** The increase to **64.3%** positions India as a leader among developing nations in terms of the rapid scale-up of **social safety floors** within a decade.
 
• **Future Projections:** The government aims to achieve near-universal coverage by **2030**, focusing on the **gig economy** and **migrant laborers** who were previously outside the formal social protection ambit.

87:T

questions.question: The city of Awaza, the venue of the Third UN Conference on Landlocked Developing Countries (2025), is located in which nation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Turkmenistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The city of **Awaza**, also known as the **Awaza National Tourist Zone**, is located in **Turkmenistan** on the eastern coast of the **Caspian Sea**.
 
• It has been officially selected as the host venue for the **Third United Nations Conference on Landlocked Developing Countries (LLDC3)**, which is scheduled to take place in **2025**.
 
• The conference was originally planned to be held in **Kigali, Rwanda**, in **2024**, but was later rescheduled and moved to **Turkmenistan** following **UN General Assembly** consultations.
 
• This high-level global summit aims to evaluate the progress of the **Vienna Programme of Action** and adopt a new **10-year** strategic document to support **landlocked developing countries** in overcoming geographical and economic hurdles.
 
• The choice of **Turkmenistan** highlights its strategic role as a major **transport and logistics hub** in **Central Asia**, facilitating trade between Europe, Asia, and the Middle East.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Turkmenistan**: It is a sovereign state in **Central Asia**, bordered by **Kazakhstan** to the northwest, **Uzbekistan** to the north and east, **Afghanistan** to the southeast, and **Iran** to the south and southwest. Its capital is **Ashgabat**.
 
• **Landlocked Developing Countries (LLDCs)**: This is a category of **32 nations** that lack direct access to the sea. These countries face higher **transaction costs** for international trade and are often dependent on transit through neighboring countries.
 
• **Awaza National Tourist Zone**: Launched in **2007**, this is a massive tourism project in the **Balkan Province** of **Turkmenistan**. It features numerous luxury hotels, resorts, and international convention centers built to host global events.
 
• **UN-OHRLLS**: The **United Nations Office of the High Representative for the Least Developed Countries, Landlocked Developing Countries and Small Island Developing States** is the lead agency coordinating the **2025** conference.
 
• **Caspian Sea**: It is the world's largest **inland body of water**, often classified as the world's largest lake or a full-fledged sea. **Turkmenistan** shares its coastline with **Russia**, **Iran**, **Azerbaijan**, and **Kazakhstan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regional Connectivity**: **Turkmenistan** has been an active proponent of **sustainable transport**, hosting the first **Global Sustainable Transport Conference** in **2016**.
 
• **Vienna Programme of Action (VPoA)**: This was a decade-long framework (**2014-2024**) designed to address the special needs of **LLDCs**; the **2025 Awaza** conference will establish the successor to this program.
 
• **Trade Challenges**: Statistics show that **LLDCs** pay more than **double** the amount that coastal developing countries pay for transport and insurance services, which the **LLDC3** summit aims to mitigate through better **digital** and **physical infrastructure**.
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**: The conference outcome will be crucial for the **2030 Agenda**, ensuring that geographically disadvantaged nations are not left behind in global development efforts.
</ul

questions.question: Announced in 2025, in which state is Similipal National Park located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Similipal National Park** is located in the **Mayurbhanj** district of the Indian state of **Odisha**. It is one of the largest national parks in India, spanning an area of approximately **2,750 square kilometers**.
 
• The name of the park is derived from the abundance of **Simul** (Red Silk Cotton) trees that bloom vividly in the region, contributing to its unique ecosystem.
 
• It was formally designated as a **Tiger Reserve** under **Project Tiger** in the year **1973**. The area was earlier a hunting ground for the royalty of **Mayurbhanj**.
 
• The government declared it a **Wildlife Sanctuary** in **1979** and subsequently a **National Park** in **1980**. It serves as a vital habitat for the **Bengal Tiger** and the **Asian Elephant**.
 
• Similipal is world-renowned for being the only natural habitat of the **Melanistic Tiger** (Black Tiger), characterized by thick black stripes due to genetic mutations. ***Hence, the correct answer is Odisha.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UNESCO Recognition**:
 
 
• In **1994**, the Government of India declared Similipal a **Biosphere Reserve**.
 
• It was added to the **UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves** in May **2009**, recognizing its global ecological significance and biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Features**:
 
 
• The park is home to some of India's most breathtaking waterfalls, including **Barehipani Falls**, which has a height of **399 meters**, and **Joranda Falls**.
 
• The terrain is characterized by high plateaus and hills, with the highest peak being **Khairiburu**, standing at an elevation of about **1,178 meters**.
 
• Several perennial rivers originate from these hills, such as the **Budhabalanga**, **Salandi**, and the **Palpala** rivers.
 
 
 
• **Flora and Fauna**:
 
 
• The park's vegetation is a rich mosaic of **Northern Tropical Moist Deciduous Forests** and **Semi-Evergreen Forests**.
 
• It boasts over **1,000 species** of plants and **96 species** of orchids. The wildlife includes **Gaur** (Indian Bison), **Chausingha** (Four-horned Antelope), **Leopard**, and over **300 species of birds** such as the **Hill Myna**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tribal Inhabitants**: The region is inhabited by several indigenous tribes, including the **Kolha**, **Santhal**, **Bhumija**, and **Mankidia**. These communities have a deep cultural and symbiotic relationship with the forest.
 
• **Conservation Efforts**: The **Mayurbhanj Elephant Reserve** includes the Similipal-Hadgarh-Kuldiha forests, forming a massive conservation landscape for **elephants** in Eastern India.
 
• **Environmental Concerns**: The park frequently faces threats from **forest fires** during the summer months (February to June) and issues related to **poaching**, which the state government of **Odisha** manages through specialized forest protection squads.
 
• **Tourism**: Entry to the park is usually regulated and remains closed during the **monsoon season** (June to October) to ensure visitor safety and allow for wildlife breeding.
</ul

questions.question: The GST Council has scraped how much percentage tax on all individual life and health insurance policies, effective 22 September 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**18%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **GST Council**, in a landmark decision, has decided to scrap the **18%** Goods and Services Tax (GST) previously levied on **individual life and health insurance** policies.
 
• This decision is set to become effective from **September 22, 2025**, aiming to provide financial relief to millions of policyholders across **India**.
 
• The move specifically targets **individual health insurance** premiums and **term life insurance** policies, ensuring that essential social security remains affordable for the common man.
 
• This policy change was recommended during the **54th GST Council Meeting**, chaired by the **Union Finance Minister**, **Nirmala Sitharaman**, following extensive deliberations by a **Group of Ministers (GoM)** on insurance rate rationalization.
 
• By removing the **18%** tax burden, the government intends to boost **insurance penetration** in the country, which is currently lower than the global average.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 18%.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **GST Council and Constitution**: 
 
 
• The **GST Council** is a constitutional body established under **Article 279A** of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• It is chaired by the **Union Finance Minister** and includes the **Union Minister of State** in charge of Revenue or Finance and Ministers in charge of Finance or Taxation of all **States**.
 
 
 
• **Significance for Senior Citizens**: 
 
 
• One of the primary beneficiaries of this exemption will be **senior citizens**, who often face high premium costs due to age-related risks. The removal of the **18%** tax significantly lowers their annual out-of-pocket expenditure.
 
 
 
• **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)**: 
 
 
• The **IRDAI**, established in **1999**, has been working towards the vision of "**Insurance for All by 2047**." Tax exemptions on premiums are seen as a critical step toward achieving this objective.
 
 
 
• **Tax Slabs in GST**: 
 
 
• Currently, **India** follows a multi-tiered tax structure for GST with slabs of **5%**, **12%**, **18%**, and **28%**. Essential services and certain food items are often placed in the **0%** (exempt) category to protect vulnerable sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Health and Life Insurance Types**: 
 
 
• **Term Insurance**: Provides pure life cover without any savings or profits component; the scraping of tax makes this primary safety net cheaper.
 
• **Health Insurance**: Covers medical expenses; the exemption is expected to encourage more individuals to opt for higher coverage amounts, such as **Rs. 5 lakh** or more, without worrying about tax inflation on the premium.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Financial Impact**: The removal of the **18%** tax is expected to result in a revenue foregone of several thousand **crores** for the government, but it is expected to be offset by the increased volume of insurance buyers.
 
• **Implementation Date**: The specific effective date of **September 22, 2025**, provides insurance companies and the **GST Network (GSTN)** sufficient time to recalibrate their systems for premium calculations.
 
• **GoM (Group of Ministers)**: The Bihar Deputy Chief Minister **Samrat Choudhary** led the **GoM** that looked into the details of these tax exemptions before the final council decision.
</ul
